proposed_amendment.rationale: 4096 is a finite bounded native allowance with headroom above1000-entry default per-mount caches, remote/control/mmap descriptor amplification and batched closes.1024 is closer to the cache count and therefore a less robust candidate without also reducing the cache. The exact value requires actual execution, not a source-derived sufficiency claim.

scope: Read-only primary-source and retained-diagnostic review. No code changes, native execution, cloud action or numerical acceptance in this review.
source_findings: --fdlimit is a native host descriptor limit applied separately to Sentry and gofer; both Cur and Max are set to the requested finite value after re-exec. It is not the guest descriptor limit.

Both native setters warn rather than abort on EPERM. Therefore command-line intent does not establish that the requested native hard limit was installed; collect /proc/<bound native pid>/limits while that actor is alive.

Guest defaults consider host RLIMIT_NOFILE, then createLimitSet explicitly overwrites defaults from OCI process.rlimits. Keeping OCI RLIMIT_NOFILE soft=hard256 preserves the guest limit when the host limit changes.
The default --dcache=-1 uses per-mount gofer caches; the default per-mount maximum is1000 cached dentries. Nonnegative --dcache selects one global gofer dentry cache initialized during mount setup.

Cache tuning is coarse, not an absolute native FD ceiling: referenced and watch-pinned dentries may not be evictable; read/write/mmap/control descriptors and other runtime descriptors exist in addition to guest-visible descriptors.
lisafs inode destruction may defer remote closes; Client.CloseFD batches up to100 queued descriptors before flushing. This adds transient native descriptor pressure beyond live guest descriptors.
